snippets: Xsight Labs, a fabless semiconductor company delivering end-to-end connectivity solutions for next-generation AI Factory, Traditional hyperscale IaaS, Next Generation Edge and private data center networks, today announced the availability of the X2, the second-generation X-Switch family of fully programmable SDN Ethernet switches.
Xsight Labs unveils the X2 — a 5nm, 12.8 Tbps fully programmable SDN switch at 200W with 40% lower power and UEC support for AI and hyperscale networks.

“X2 supports a broad range of SKUs from 3.2Tbps at 140W to 12.8Tbps at 200W,” said Gal Malach, Co-Founder and CTO at Xsight Labs, “This provides hyperscale and enterprise cloud customers with an extensive portfolio of programmable, power-efficient and cost-effective switches for their 25G, 50G and 100G SerDes-based connectivity requirements.” · The X-Switch family delivers application-optimized switching for the 100G SerDes ecosystem. The X2 is a scalable, power-efficient, flexible solution supporting advanced features like congestion-aware routing, fast link recovery, and Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) compliance to improve the overall efficiency of the network for AI workloads.

The X2 enables best-in-class network visibility empowering operators to troubleshoot network failures with little to no downtime, leading to CapEx/OpEx savings for cloud service providers and edge operators. ... web.description: Xsight Labs, an innovator in high-performance connectivity silicon, today announced that Starlink, the world’s most advanced satellite constellation in low-Earth orbit, delivering broadband, will leverage the Xsight X2 Programmable Ethernet switch to serve as the high speed networking core ...
snippets: Xsight Labs, an innovator in high-performance connectivity silicon, today announced that Starlink, the world’s most advanced satellite constellation in low-Earth orbit, delivering broadband, will leverage the Xsight X2 Programmable Ethernet switch to serve as the high speed networking core for its next-generation Starlink V3 satellites.
Xsight’s X2 powers next‑gen Starlink V3 satellites with 12.8T switching, ultra‑low‑power performance, and fully programmable networking for orbital workloads.

The X2 delivers 12.8 Tbps of switching capacity using state of the art 100G SerDes and TSMC’s N5 process, providing a power-efficient, ultra-low-latency data path built for harsh environments. Its fully programmable architecture allows it to dynamically adapt to evolving orbital networking demands, ensuring optimal performance across a wide range of satellite workloads.
X2’s flexible, programmable architecture adapts seamlessly to diverse orbital and ground-based networking workloads

snippets: The X2 12.8T fully programmable switch is available now and delivers transformative benefits, including reduced latency, lower power consumption, and decreased TCO. Complementing the X2 Switch, Xsight Labs also offers the E1, a 5nm 800G DPU designed for open, Linux-based SDN environments. By breaking away from proprietary norms, Xsight Labs is paving the way for a new era of openness, collaboration, and innovation in Ethernet switching — rearchitecting the foundation of cloud and AI infrastructure.
Xsight Labs opens its X-Series switch Instruction Set Architecture (XISA) — an industry first enabling full switch programmability and ecosystem collaboration.
The X-Switch architecture represents a paradigm shift in Ethernet switch design, combining fine-grained programmability with unparalleled flexibility and efficiency.

This move aims to enhance network performance and development productivity by granting customers and partners full transparency into the behavior of switch chips – long regarded as “black boxes” that stifled innovation. “We at Oxide believe in programmable networking silicon but have been frustrated by vendors’ insistence on keeping their instruction set architectures secret,” said Bryan Cantrill, Co-Founder and CTO, Oxide Computer Company.
